# ha-gatekeeper -- Complete Documentation

> A reliability-first MCP server for Home Assistant implementing the "LLM as an untrusted advisor" architecture. The LLM generates intent; a deterministic policy engine decides whether that intent is permitted.

## Overview

ha-gatekeeper interposes a four-tier deterministic policy engine between an LLM and Home Assistant. Unlike existing HA MCP servers that execute LLM tool calls directly against HA with no authorisation layer, ha-gatekeeper classifies, authorises, rate-limits, and audits every action.

Key properties:
- If ha-gatekeeper crashes, Home Assistant continues to function normally. The LLM layer is additive, never load-bearing.
- Unclassified entities default to Tier 3 (prohibited). The system fails closed.
- Entity IDs are validated against live HA state with fuzzy matching. Hallucinated entities are rejected with suggestions for similar entity names, enabling LLM self-correction.
- All Tier 1+ actions are recorded in a SHA-256 hash-chained SQLite audit log with before/after entity state. Each row includes a hash of the previous row, making the trail tamper-evident.
- Implements four layers from the "Verified Autonomy: A Field Guide to Engineering Trust in AI Systems" (Newman & Greene, 2026) trust architecture.

Tech stack: TypeScript (strict mode), Node.js >= 20, MCP SDK v1.x (Streamable HTTP transport), home-assistant-js-websocket, better-sqlite3, Zod, pino, prom-client, Express.

---

## Architecture

Four-layer design:

1. MCP Server (Layer 1): Tool registry (15 curated tools), entity validator, request context builder.
2. Policy Engine (Layer 2): Tier resolver, rate limiter, range clamper, HITL confirmation.
3. Execution Engine (Layer 3): HA WebSocket client, state capture with 500ms settling delay, three-state circuit breaker.
4. Observability (Layer 4): SQLite audit log, Prometheus metrics, health check endpoint.

Request flow: MCP tool call -> entity validation (does entity exist in HA? fuzzy match suggestions if not) -> tier resolution (entity -> tier 0-3) -> policy constraints (rate limit, range clamp, confirmation) -> execution via HA WebSocket -> state capture (before/after) -> hash-chained audit log -> return result.

---

## Verified Autonomy Layer Mapping

Implements four layers from "Verified Autonomy: A Field Guide to Engineering Trust in AI Systems" (Newman & Greene, 2026):

Layer 03 (Making Failures Visible): Entity validation with Levenshtein-distance fuzzy matching. Hallucinated entity names return up to 3 suggestions from the same domain, enabling LLM self-correction. Tracked by ha_gatekeeper_entity_hallucinations_total metric.

Layer 05 (Deterministic Guardrails): Four-tier policy engine. "The model proposes. The rule decides." Maps to the Field Guide's three-severity model (INFO, WARN, BLOCK) plus a read-only tier.

Layer 08 (Cryptographic Audit Trails): Each audit row includes a SHA-256 hash (row_hash) and a reference to the previous row's hash (previous_hash). First row uses "GENESIS". The verify_audit_integrity tool checks the entire chain for tampering.

Layer 02 (Outlier Detection as Hard Escalation): Circuit breaker triggers independently on any failure signal. Fails safe by design.

---

## Policy Tiers

Tier 0 (Unrestricted): Execute immediately, no audit log entry. Used for read-only queries.
- Default domains: sensor.*, binary_sensor.*, weather.*, sun.*, person.*
- Default actions: homeassistant.get_state, homeassistant.get_states, homeassistant.get_entity, homeassistant.search

Tier 1 (Logged): Execute and write full audit trail with before/after state. Rate limiting applied.
- Default domains: light.*, switch.*, media_player.*, fan.*, cover.*, input_boolean.*, input_number.*, scene.*
- Default rate limit: 10 calls per entity per minute

Tier 2 (Confirmed): Requires human approval before execution. Rate limiting, range clamping, and confirmation applied.
- Default domains: climate.*, lock.*, alarm_control_panel.*, valve.*, humidifier.*
- Default rate limit: 3 calls per entity per minute
- Confirmation via HA notification service with configurable timeout (default 30s)
- Range clamping enforces hard min/max on numeric values (e.g. temperature 15-25C)

Tier 3 (Prohibited): Deterministically blocked. The attempt is always logged. Never executed.
- Default domains: automation.*, script.*, input_button.*
- Default actions: homeassistant.restart, homeassistant.reload_*, backup.*
- Returns: "This action is not permitted by policy. Entity [X] is classified as Tier 3 (Prohibited)."

### Tier Resolution Order

Resolution is deterministic. The first match in this order wins:
1. entity_overrides map (specific entity_id -> tier)
2. tiers[n].entities lists (specific entity_id within a tier definition)
3. tiers[n].domains patterns (domain wildcards like light.*)
4. tiers[n].actions patterns (action wildcards like homeassistant.reload_*)
5. default_tier (fallback, default: 3)

Entity-level overrides always take precedence over domain rules. Example: light.nursery can be promoted to Tier 2 even though light.* is Tier 1.

---

## Tools

15 curated tools organised by user intent:

### Read Tools (Tier 0)
- get_entity_state: Get current state and attributes of one entity. Input: entity_id.
- list_entities: List entities with optional domain/area/label filter. Input: domain?, area?, label?.
- get_area_summary: Get all devices and states in an area. Input: area.
- get_home_summary: High-level summary of the entire home state. No input required.
- get_entity_history: State history for an entity over a time range. Input: entity_id, start_time?, end_time?.

### Control Tools (Tier depends on target entity)
- turn_on: Turn on a light, switch, fan, media player, etc. Input: entity_id.
- turn_off: Turn off a device. Input: entity_id.
- toggle: Toggle device state. Input: entity_id.
- set_value: Set a numeric value (brightness, temperature, volume, position). Input: entity_id, attribute, value.
- activate_scene: Activate a predefined scene. Input: entity_id.
- send_command: Domain-specific command (e.g. media_player.play_media). Input: domain, service, entity_id?, service_data?.

### Monitoring Tools
- get_anomalies: Analyse current home state and report anomalies.
- get_policy_summary: Show current policy tiers and entity classifications.

### Meta Tools
- get_server_health: Return health status, circuit breaker state, recent error rates.
- verify_audit_integrity: Verify the hash chain of the audit log. Checks that no entries have been tampered with.

All tools use Zod input schemas. Read tools are annotated with readOnlyHint: true. Control tools with tier >= 2 are annotated with destructiveHint: true.

---

## Configuration

Single YAML file (config.yaml) with environment variable substitution (${VAR_NAME} syntax).

### homeassistant section
- url (string, required): WebSocket URL, e.g. ws://homeassistant.local:8123/api/websocket
- token (string, required): Long-lived access token. Use ${HA_TOKEN} for env var.
- reconnect_interval_ms (integer, optional, default 5000): Ms between reconnection attempts.
- max_reconnect_attempts (integer, optional, default 10): Max consecutive reconnection attempts.

### server section
- port (integer, required): MCP transport port (default 8200).
- host (string, required): Bind address (default 0.0.0.0).
- transport (string, required): "streamable-http" or "stdio".
- session_mode (string, optional, default "stateful"): "stateful" or "stateless".

### policy section
- default_tier (0-3, required): Fallback tier. Use 3 to fail closed.
- tiers: Map of tier number (0-3) to tier config.
  - description (string, required): Human-readable description.
  - domains (string[], optional): Domain wildcard patterns.
  - entities (string[], optional): Specific entity IDs.
  - actions (string[], optional): Action patterns.
  - constraints (object, optional):
    - rate_limit.max_calls_per_entity_per_minute (integer)
    - confirmation.method ("notification" or "webhook")
    - confirmation.timeout_seconds (integer)
    - confirmation.notification_service (string, e.g. notify.mobile_app_ant)
    - confirmation.message_template (string, supports {{action}} and {{entity_id}})
    - range_clamp: Map of "domain.attribute" to {min, max}.
- entity_overrides: Map of entity_id to tier number. Highest priority in resolution.

### circuit_breaker section
- health_check_interval_ms (integer, required): Ms between health checks when circuit is open.
- failure_threshold (integer, required): Consecutive failures to trip.
- recovery_threshold (integer, required): Consecutive successes to reset from half-open.
- timeout_ms (integer, required): Max time for any HA API call.

### observability section
- audit_log.enabled (boolean), audit_log.database (string, SQLite path), audit_log.retention_days (integer)
- metrics.enabled (boolean), metrics.port (integer, Prometheus scrape endpoint)
- health.enabled (boolean), health.port (integer, health check endpoint)

### Environment Variables
- HA_TOKEN: Home Assistant long-lived access token (required)
- HA_SENTINEL_CONFIG: Path to config YAML file (default ./config.yaml)
- HA_SENTINEL_LOG_LEVEL: debug | info | warn | error (default info)
- NODE_ENV: Runtime environment (default production)

---

## Circuit Breaker

Three states: CLOSED (normal), OPEN (tripped), HALF_OPEN (testing recovery).

CLOSED: All requests flow through. Failures increment a counter. Any success resets the counter. If counter >= failure_threshold, transition to OPEN.

OPEN: All control tool calls return a circuit breaker error. Read tools may still function. After health_check_interval_ms, attempt a health check (get_config call). If it succeeds, transition to HALF_OPEN.

HALF_OPEN: Limited requests allowed. If recovery_threshold consecutive successes, transition to CLOSED. Any failure transitions back to OPEN.

---

## Audit Log

SQLite database with the following schema:

Columns: id (INTEGER PK), timestamp (TEXT ISO 8601), request_id (TEXT UUID), tool_name (TEXT), entity_id (TEXT), action (TEXT), parameters (TEXT JSON), policy_tier (INTEGER 0-3), policy_decision (TEXT: allowed|denied_rate_limit|denied_prohibited|denied_timeout|confirmed|clamped), clamped_from (TEXT JSON), clamped_to (TEXT JSON), state_before (TEXT JSON), state_after (TEXT JSON), execution_duration_ms (INTEGER), error (TEXT), llm_rationale (TEXT), row_hash (TEXT SHA-256), previous_hash (TEXT SHA-256 or "GENESIS"), created_at (TEXT).

Indexes on: timestamp, entity_id, policy_decision.
Retention: configurable, default 90 days.

---

## Prometheus Metrics

Exposed at GET /metrics on the configured port (default 9090):

- ha_gatekeeper_tool_calls_total (counter, labels: tool, tier, decision)
- ha_gatekeeper_tool_call_duration_seconds (histogram, labels: tool)
- ha_gatekeeper_circuit_breaker_state (gauge, 0=closed, 1=half_open, 2=open)
- ha_gatekeeper_rate_limit_rejections_total (counter, labels: entity_id)
- ha_gatekeeper_entity_hallucinations_total (counter)
- ha_gatekeeper_confirmation_timeouts_total (counter)
- ha_gatekeeper_ha_connection_state (gauge, 0=disconnected, 1=connected)
- ha_gatekeeper_policy_denials_total (counter, labels: tier, reason)

---

## Health Check

GET /health on the configured port (default 8201):

Response: { status, circuit_breaker, ha_connected, ha_entity_count, uptime_seconds, last_tool_call, error_rate_1h, version }

Status values: "healthy" (breaker closed + HA connected), "degraded" (breaker half-open), "unhealthy" (breaker open or HA disconnected).

---

## Project Structure

```
src/
  index.ts                     Entry point: config load, HA connect, server start
  logger.ts                    Pino logger instance
  config/
    schema.ts                  Zod schema for config.yaml
    loader.ts                  YAML loading + ${ENV_VAR} substitution
    defaults.ts                Default config values
  server/
    mcp-server.ts              McpServer setup and transport
    entity-validator.ts        Fuzzy matching entity validation (Levenshtein distance)
    tools/
      index.ts                 Tool registry
      read-tools.ts            get_entity_state, list_entities, get_area_summary, get_home_summary, get_entity_history
      control-tools.ts         turn_on, turn_off, toggle, set_value, activate_scene, send_command
      monitoring-tools.ts      get_anomalies, get_policy_summary
      meta-tools.ts            get_server_health, verify_audit_integrity
  policy/
    engine.ts                  Policy evaluation orchestrator
    tier-resolver.ts           Entity/action -> tier number
    rate-limiter.ts            Per-entity sliding window
    range-clamper.ts           Numeric value clamping
    confirmation.ts            HITL confirmation flow
  execution/
    ha-client.ts               HA WebSocket connection (home-assistant-js-websocket)
    state-capture.ts           Before/after state with 500ms settling delay
    circuit-breaker.ts         Three-state circuit breaker
  observability/
    audit-log.ts               SQLite audit log (better-sqlite3, WAL mode)
    metrics.ts                 Prometheus metrics (prom-client)
    health.ts                  Health check endpoint (Express)
  types/
    ha.ts                      HA API types (EntityState, HAServiceCall, etc.)
    policy.ts                  Policy types (PolicyTier, PolicyDecision, TierConfig, etc.)
    audit.ts                   Audit log entry type
    tools.ts                   Tool I/O types
tests/
  unit/                        Mirrors src/ structure
  integration/                 Full pipeline tests
  fixtures/                    Test config YAML, mock entity JSON
```

---

## Development

Commands:
- npm run build: TypeScript compilation (strict mode, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes)
- npm run dev: Hot reload development mode (tsx watch)
- npm run lint: ESLint with strict TypeScript rules
- npm run test: Vitest (unit + integration)
- npm start: Run compiled server

Coding standards:
- British English throughout
- Conventional commits (feat:, fix:, chore:, refactor:, test:, docs:)
- No `any` type without inline justification
- No console.log (use pino logger)
- No empty catch blocks
- JSDoc on all public functions
- Tests required for every new module

TypeScript config: target ES2022, module NodeNext, strict: true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true, exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true.

---

## Deployment

Docker multi-stage build. Runs as non-root user (gatekeeper). Exposes ports 8200 (MCP), 8201 (health), 8202 (confirmation webhook), 9090 (metrics). Health check via wget to /health endpoint. Data volume for SQLite audit database.

Docker Compose provided with config.yaml mounted read-only, HA_TOKEN via environment variable, restart unless-stopped policy.
